O.outcome_detail: student-reported usefulness for acquiring and consolidating subject knowledge

cells.quote: The results of the survey indicate a positive response to the Computer Science practical lesson, with high percentages of agreement on various aspects: 94.6% found the lesson important and 85.7% and 83.9% found it useful for acquiring and consolidating subject knowledge, respectively.
cells.note: The voluntary anonymous survey reported favorable percentages but did not include a comparison condition or baseline.

O.outcome_detail: self-reported information-finding, use and management skills

cells.quote: In addition, 89.3% felt that the lessons were effective in helping them to learn how to find, use and manage information, and a substantial majority of 87.5% considered the assessment system to be appropriate.
cells.note: This was a post-activity self-report without a comparison group or pre-intervention measure.

result.effect: 64.3% met the set standards; 35.7% did not

cells.quote: In this sense, this didactic proposal proved to be effective in most cases, with 64.3% (60.3% for 2020/21 and 68.6% for 2021/22) of students demonstrating knowledge and skills that met the set standards, compared to 35.7% (39.7% for 2020/21 and 31.4% for 2021/22) who did not meet the minimum requirements and needed significant support (Figure 7a).
cells.note: The study reports achievement distributions against rubric standards, not against a separate comparison condition.

O.outcome_detail: final-report qualification levels across academic years

cells.quote: Since the p-value is greater than the significance level of 0.05, there were no significant differences between the qualifications of the different academic years.
cells.note: The academic-year comparison was non-significant; no power or equivalence test was reported.
